caution_note: They are not interchangeable one-for-one in every recipe.

caution_note: They often need bulking agents when replacing sugar in foods.

display_note: These polyols add sweetness and bulk with different digestion and texture properties.
caution_note: Large amounts can affect digestion for some people; xylitol is dangerous to dogs.

display_note: Different acids create different styles of sourness and acidity balance.
caution_note: They are not identical in flavor strength or food behavior.

display_note: Leavening systems create rise in baked goods.
caution_note: Substitution changes rise timing flavor and sodium or phosphate content.

display_note: Emulsifiers help fats water and air stay distributed in foods.
caution_note: Source and allergen status can vary.

display_note: These ingredients control thickness suspension and gel texture.
caution_note: Texture effects differ dramatically by amount and food type.

display_note: Plant proteins differ in texture flavor allergen profile and amino-acid balance.
caution_note: Soy wheat and legume sensitivities should be surfaced clearly.

display_note: Dairy proteins add nutrition texture and body.
Gluten-free flours usually need blends to mimic wheat flour structure.
Starches thicken sauces and improve texture in baked foods.
caution_note: Different starches thicken at different rates and textures.

display_note: Neutral oils provide fat with mild flavor.
caution_note: Smoke point and fatty acid profile vary by refinement and type.

caution_note: Dietary religious allergen and saturated fat considerations vary.
